subject: AWS Marketplace co-sell: buyer approval windows, term-length options, and pricing structure
messages:
From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cloudbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Sullivan <amy.sullivan@amazon.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Marketplace purchase path + approvals for co-sell

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is starting to scope the purchase and asked for clarification on two items so we can move to our internal approvals:

1) Term length options in AWS Marketplace private offers — do you support 12 / 24 / 36 month PO lengths, and how do discounts layer with longer commitments?
2) Buyer approval gating — our legal/procurement team needs the exact list of buyer-side approvers and expected timelines for Marketplace PO acceptance (e.g., buyer PO, AWS private offer acceptance window, seller counter-sign). Any docs you can share help us map to internal milestones.

Can Amy also confirm if co-sell crediting changes the approval flow on the AWS side?

Appreciate any examples or a short matrix — procurement would like to review by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Sarah Tan
Head of Finance Operations
CloudBridge, Inc.

--
Attachment: procurement_template_blank.xlsx (referenced)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Amy Sullivan <amy.sullivan@amazon.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace purchase path + approvals for co-sell

Hi Sarah —

Great to hear procurement is lining this up. High-level answers below, and I attached a concise term/pricing matrix for your team. Quick summary:

- Term lengths: We commonly support 12, 24, and 36 month private offers. 12 and 24 month PO flows are straightforward in AWS Marketplace; 36-month offers are supported but require an additional buyer confirmation step in their procurement system and are treated as a longer-term commitment for accounting.
- Pricing/discounting: We offer baseline list pricing (monthly metered or annual upfront). Discounts increase with commitment length and upfront payment: typical matrix in the attached sheet (rows = term, columns = list price, prepay 12mo, prepay 36mo).
- Buyer approvals and windows: AWS private offer acceptance window is typically 30 days from the offer link, but buyers often route internally and request 45–60 days for larger deals. Key buyer approvers we see: procurement lead, legal counsel, finance approver, cost center owner. On the seller side, Redwood issues the private-offer in AWS and tracks acceptance.

Amy — if you have any AWS-specific timing notes for co-sell crediting, please add.

If this works, we can propose a mutual action plan (MAP) and a sample DocuSign flow to align timelines.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_marketplace_term_matrix_v3.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cloudbridge.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace purchase path + approvals for co-sell

Sarah —

Adding a couple of practical notes from pricing/ops perspective:

- Discount bands: For reference, our standard bands are ~10% off list for 12mo prepaid, 18% for 24mo prepaid, and up to 28% for 36mo prepaid (depends on committed seat/token volume). We can carve out a custom ramp for initial year + steady-state pricing; happy to model this for your expected usage.
- AWS steps: We typically create the private offer, then buyer completes acceptance in the AWS Console. For co-sell opportunities where AWS is engaged, the AWS Partner Manager usually confirms co-sell attribution within 5 business days after acceptance — that attribution speeds certain marketplace procurement handoffs.
- Approvals doc: Attached is our co-sell eligibility checklist and a short procurement playbook that maps internal approver roles to expected artifacts (SOC2 audit, data flow diagram, encryption attestation).

If procurement wants, Karthik can run a short spreadsheet showing monthly cost delta between 12/24/36month prepay vs monthly metered.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: co-sell-eligibility-checklist.pdf

From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@cloudbridge.com>

Date: 2027-04-19T14:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace purchase path + approvals for co-sell

Thanks Vivek and Vanessa — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal after reviewing the attachments:

- They need a short statement confirming Redwood's data-retention policy for marketplace customers and whether logs are included in the retention window. Also: confirmation of SOC 2 type II status and where to find the audit report or an auditor's contact.
- For 36-month offers: finance asked whether Redwood will allow an annual true-up if actual usage is materially lower/higher than committed tokens.
- Can you provide a sample buyer approval cadence we can include in our MAP? We need a 4–6 week internal timeline with milestones we can attach to our PO.

Procurement asked for a working call Friday afternoon if you have 30 minutes to finalize the MAP and pre-sign docs. Amy — would it make sense for your team to join to confirm co-sell timing?

Regards,
Sarah

Sarah —

Thanks — we can cover everything on Friday. Proposed 30-minute agenda:

1) Confirmation of term options + discount band to be included in PO (Vivek/Vanessa)
2) Buyer-side approval cadence and expected approvers (Procurement) — we'll provide a template MAP with milestones
3) Co-sell attribution & AWS timing (Amy)
4) Operational asks: SOC2 evidence, data-retention statement, invoice cadence, and sample DocuSign flow (Karthik)

Quick answers inline to your asks:
- SOC2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified. We will share the auditor access link and an NDA'd copy of the report during procurement review.
- Data-retention: We retain customer logs for 90 days by default; configurable longer retention is available on Dedicated/Private deployments and can be added to the PO as an addendum. Logs used for billing are retained for 24 months.
- 36-month true-up: We support an annual true-up clause for committed usage with a +/- 20% threshold before true-up fees apply. We can include this in the PO language.

DocuSign link to a draft private-offer acceptance plus signature blocks: https://www.docusign.com/link/abcd-aws-po-rdw

Please confirm a time Friday 16:00 ET / 13:00 PT and we'll send a calendar invite. If procurement prefers earlier, we have 10am ET available as well.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
